question_text: A 74-year-old man presents with complaints of sudden severe crushing retrosternal pain. The pain radiated to his left arm shortly after it began, and he was subsequently rushed to the emergency department for evaluation. His troponins and creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) were elevated. Unfortunately, the patient died within the next 2 hours and an autopsy was performed immediately. The gross examination of the heart will show?

                    ### Question
                    A 74-year-old man presents with complaints of sudden severe crushing retrosternal pain. The pain radiated to his left arm shortly after it began, and he was subsequently rushed to the emergency department for evaluation. His troponins and creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) were elevated. Unfortunately, the patient died within the next 2 hours and an autopsy was performed immediately. The gross examination of the heart will show?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Abundant neutrophils
opb. Red granulation tissue surrounding the infarction
opc. Normal heart tissue
opd. White, patchy, non-contractile scar
ope. Pallor of the infarcted tissue

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the setting of acute myocardial infarction, the gross examination of the heart in this patient would likely show red granulation tissue surrounding the infarction, which eventually progresses to white, patchy, non-contractile scar formation. The presence of abundant neutrophils would not be expected in the gross examination of the heart tissue post-infarction.
